# The base build, seeded worktrees and the old code

**seeding**
: Making a worktree with a copy of the build and caches of a built, clean worktree. `seed-worktree.sh` makes the copy and rewrites the paths in it (`SKILL.md`, "The caches").

**base build**
: Clean worktree at the base, built in place by ant, or seeded. Every other worktree is seeded from it.

**old code**
: Base's code, run from the base build with a private caches folder.

Once the base build is built, run its code only as "Running the old code" says, with a private caches folder outside it. Any other run writes into the caches that every worktree is seeded from.

## Finding or building a base build

- If your brief names a base build, use it.
- If not, look in `git worktree list`. Earlier base builds are at paths such as `/home/user/fortress-base<N>`. A worktree can be your base build if it passes three checks:
  - `git -C <it> rev-parse HEAD` prints your base;
  - `git -C <it> status --porcelain` prints nothing;
  - it holds `default_repository/caches/bytecode_cache/fortress.CompilerBuiltin.jar`.
- If no worktree passes them, build one at a path of your own, outside the main tree. It takes about 200 s: start the build and the library order detached, with the `nohup` line of `session.md`, "Long commands". `<base-commit>` is your base: the commit that your brief names, else your tree's `HEAD` when you start. Say so in your report.

      git worktree add --detach <base-build> <base-commit>
      cd <base-build>          # then set up the call as build-and-caches.md says
      ant compileAll
      # then the library order (build-and-caches.md), then this walk run, which warms walk's caches:
      bin/fortress ProjectFortress/tests/BooleanOps.fss
      git status --porcelain   # must print nothing: the seeding script refuses a base build that is not clean

If you check a fix against its old code, use a base build at the commit that the fix starts from. If a brief names the fix's base, the fix starts there. If not, the fix starts from `git merge-base <its branch> main`, or from the parent of its first commit on `main`.

## Seeding a worktree

A build, and a run of `bin/fortress` without a private caches folder, walk's too, write into the caches of the tree that they run in. So build and run only in a tree whose caches no other agent uses. Your brief says where you work. If your work builds or runs code and your brief gives you no tree of your own, seed a worktree of your own instead of building one. Then work only there.

Seeding takes about 3 s and 206 MB of disk. The new worktree runs walk and the compiled path right away, with the library already compiled.

    explorations/coordinator/tools/seed-worktree.sh <base-build> <new-worktree> <branch> [<start-point>]

- The script checks out `<branch>`: a local branch, else origin's, else a new branch cut from `<start-point>`, by default the base build's commit. With `-`, it makes a detached worktree at `<start-point>`.
- If the script exits 2, the base build is not built or not clean, and the script made nothing. Then make the worktree with `git worktree add`, build it yourself, and say so in your report.
- If the worktree already exists, the script keeps its branch. If it already has a build, the script keeps that too. `SEED_FORCE=1` replaces it.
- If you start in a worktree that has no build, seed it in place: name it as `<new-worktree>`, and its branch as `<branch>`.
- The script lists the library sources that differ from the base build's commit. Before a compiled run, take for each the step that `build-and-caches.md`, "After an edit of the library", gives.
- If the script warns that the copied build is the base's, run `ant compileAll`, then the library order. Without the warning, `ant compileAll` keeps the seeded caches.
- If another agent seeded your worktree, make the script's two lists yourself: `git diff --name-only <base> -- Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin` for the library sources, and `git diff --name-only <base> -- ProjectFortress/src ProjectFortress/astgen build.xml` for the warning.
- Reuse another tree's build or caches only through this script.

## Running the old code

If your worktree holds an edit and you need the base's behaviour, run the old code instead of reverting your edit. For example, see a test fail, or compare a program's old and new output.

`old-fortress.sh` runs the base build's `bin/fortress`. It sets `FORTRESS_HOME` to the base build and `FORTRESS_CACHES` to the private caches folder that you name, over your settings. Name a folder inside your worktree's `tmp/`:

    OLD=explorations/coordinator/tools/old-fortress.sh
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches compile P.fss     # the compiled path ...
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches run P             # ... then the run
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches P.fss             # walk
    $OLD <base-build> <worktree>/tmp/old-caches junit <worktree>/ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/X.test [Y.test ...]   # compiled .test files, in one JVM

- Any copy of the tool works, because it runs the base build that its first argument names.
- On first use, it fills the private folder with a copy of the base build's caches (36 MB, 0.04 s). Later runs use the same folder.
- Every cache file that a run writes goes to the private folder, and nothing else that it writes under the base build stays. So several agents can run the old code at once.
- Keep your programs outside the base build too, because a program writes its own logs beside it. The tool refuses a private folder inside the base build (exit 2).

To run interpreter tests on the old code, run the base build's `harness-one.sh` with `FORTRESS_HOME` set to the base build:

    FORTRESS_HOME=<base-build> <base-build>/explorations/compile-ladder/rung-inference-walk/harness-one.sh \
        <worktree>/tmp/old-harness <worktree>/ProjectFortress/tests/X.fss

The `run` step of a compiled `.test` is a separate `bin/fortress run` process. It inherits `FORTRESS_HOME` and `FORTRESS_CACHES`, and takes its class path from `FORTRESS_CACHES`. If you compose a harness run by hand with `-Dfortress.caches=<folder>`, set `FORTRESS_CACHES` to the same folder. Otherwise the `run` step fails with "Could not load ... Resource not found".
# Running tests

**track**
: One of the four JVMs of `ant testFast`.

**shard**
: One of the four JVMs of `ant testSystem`. Shard i of n takes every n-th file of the sorted list, from index i.

**code state**
: Code of a tree as one edit leaves it. Only an edit of code makes a new code state; a commit does not.

## The two suites

`ant testFast` runs about 1,800 tests in four tracks at once, in about 9 to 11 minutes:

- compiler: `CompilerJUTest` over `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/` and `parser_tests/`. It is the longest track, so it sets the total time.
- library: `LibraryJUTest` over `library_tests/`.
- othercompiler: `OtherCompilerJUTest` over `other_compiler_tests/`.
- misc: the unit `*JUTest` classes.

`ant testSystem` runs `SystemJUTest` over `ProjectFortress/tests/`, the interpreter's test folder. It runs about 500 tests in four shards, in about 2 to 4 minutes.

`ant testSpecData` runs the specification's 130 extracted examples (`SpecData/examples/basic`, `preliminaries`, `advanced`) under walk, in under a minute. The gate runs it after the two suites.

The newest gate summary has the exact counts and times of the last landed run:

    git log -1 --name-only --format= -- 'explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-*/gate/summary.txt'

The two suites work in the same way:

- Each suite runs `ant compileAll` first, as every `ant` test target does, so it never tests stale classes. After an edit of Java or Scala, that build empties `default_repository/caches` (`build-and-caches.md`, "Building"). Each analyses or compiles the Fortress code that it tests, in private caches.
- Each JVM gets 768 MB, a 32 MB stack and `FORTRESS_THREADS=4`, whatever the shell exports. The run steps of the compiled tests get `JAVA_FLAGS=-Xmx4g -Xss64m`, also whatever the shell exports.
- Each suite deletes `ProjectFortress/test-caches` when it starts. Each JVM keeps its caches in a folder of its own under it, so that the JVMs do not overwrite each other's entries. Temporary files go to `ProjectFortress/test-tmp/`.
- The results are in `ProjectFortress/TEST-RESULTS/fast-<track>/` and `system-<i>/`, as `TEST-<class>.txt`.

To run a suite:

- Run one suite at a time in a tree, because each suite deletes the `test-caches` that the other uses.
- Read the verdict in the line before `Total time:`: `BUILD SUCCESSFUL` means zero failures, and `BUILD FAILED` means at least one. Every `ant` test target ends with these lines, and exits non-zero when it failed.
- To compare test counts, compare the sum of the four shards. A file added to `tests/` moves every later file to another shard.
- If a suite's count fell, a `.test` file or a `tests=` line almost always went missing.

## The switches that the harness reads

Put a `-D` switch on the `java` line of a run by hand; the `java` line in `harness-one.sh` is a model. On the `ant` line, it does not reach the suites' JVMs.

- `-Dtests=<dir>`: the folder that `SystemJUTest` runs, in place of `tests/`.
- `-Dfortress.suite.shard=i/n`: run shard i of n only.
- `-Dfortress.unittests.count=N`: run N files at most.
- `-Dfortress.unittests.seed=<value>`: the order of the files. Each run prints its seed as `FORTRESS_UNITTESTS_SEED=...`.
- `FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1` for `SystemJUTest`, `-Dfortress.junit.verbose=true` for the compiled tests' classes: show the output of passing tests too.
- `-Dfortress.junit.reset=false`: `CompilerJUTest` and `LibraryJUTest` keep their caches folder. Without it, they empty it when they start.

## Outside the gate

- `ant testNotPassing` runs the interpreter programs of `ProjectFortress/not_passing_yet/`, which are expected to fail. It fails if one of them passes.
- Nothing runs these folders: `not_working_compiler_tests/`, `not_working_library_tests/`, `not_working_static_tests/`, `obsolete_interpreter_tests/`, `long_term_not_working/`, `linker_tests/`, `compiler_regressions/`. Put every new test in a gated test folder. A test of a defect that fails today is an `XXX` test there (`tests-writing.md`).

## When to run a whole suite

- The gate runs every suite once, on the tree that lands (`gate.md`). Your brief says whether you run the gate.
- If your edit changes the Java or Scala of the checker, of walk or of a phase that both paths share, run all the tests that it reaches. Run them once, after your last edit of code. The run needs no commit.
  - For the checker, run `ant testQuick`: the compiler, othercompiler and library tracks at once (below).
  - For walk, run `ant testSystem`. It is the same as its four shards run by hand.
  - For a shared phase (under `compiler/`: name binding, DSL grammars, desugaring, the marking of overloaded calls in `OverloadRewriter`) or the parser, run both.
- Quote the verdict lines and the command in your report, with the commit if your code is committed.
- If the gate later runs on a tree that holds other changes too, that tree is another code state. Your run and the gate's run do not repeat each other.
- After an edit of the code generator (`codegen/`, `OverloadSet`) or the run time (`runtimeSystem/`), run your own tests, and the four-thread atomic runs (`gate.md`) if `compiler.md` asks for them. Leave the whole tracks to the gate.
- After every other change, run only your own tests, through the scripts below. Leave the rest to the gate. This includes an edit of either library, though it reaches many tests.

The suites do not check these:

- the bytecode optimizer, which nothing in the compiler calls;
- DSL grammars, except one program whose phases the misc track runs: `syntax_abstraction_tests/ForUse.fss`;
- the linker's aliasing of apis;
- `fortress unparse`;
- the round trip of the `.tfi` and `.tfs` caches;
- a behaviour above one thread that one run of each suite at four threads does not hit.

If your edit is in one of these, your own tests are its only check. Say so in your report.

#!/bin/bash
# junit.sh <label> <dir-of-tests> <Name.test>... : the gather of climb batch N runs each .test through the
# harness in the main tree (fortress junit, the compiled test harness, as climb batch 6.5's gather ran its pair),
# in the order given, so that a link test runs before its XXX run test. Each named component's cache entries are
# removed before the list and after it. First line: the machine line (protocol.md, principle 2).
# ONE_JVM=1 (added 2026-09-29 for the repair on the merged tree, coordinator/climb-batch-workflow.md, "A repair
# of tests and records only"): the whole list in one fortress junit run, one JVM, as the gate's track runs them
# together; Shell junit hands the list to FileTests.suiteFromListOfFiles (Shell.java:1086), which puts its
# compile and link tests before its run tests (FileTests.java:997-1004), so a link test still runs first.
# The environment is env.sh's, set here without sourcing it, since env.sh also removes parser directories in
# /tmp. The tree is the one this script is in. FORTRESS_THREADS=4 is the pin of build.xml's fastTrack macro,
# which runs the gate's compiled tracks. The JVMs keep their temporary files, parser directories among them,
# in the tree's tmp/.
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-25-openjdk-amd64
export PATH="$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH"
export FORTRESS_HOME="$(cd "$(dirname "$0")/../../../.." && pwd)"
unset JAVA_TOOL_OPTIONS
export FORTRESS_THREADS=4
mkdir -p "$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
export JAVA_FLAGS="-Xmx4g -Xss64m -Djava.io.tmpdir=$FORTRESS_HOME/tmp"
FH=$FORTRESS_HOME; L=${1:?label}; D=$(cd "${2:?dir}" && pwd); shift 2
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress"
CP=$(../bin/fortress_classpath | tail -1)
echo "# junit.sh $L $(date -u +%FT%TZ); nproc $(nproc); $(grep -m1 'model name' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //'); $(grep -m1 'cpu MHz' /proc/cpuinfo | cut -d: -f2 | sed 's/^ //') MHz; load at start $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=$FORTRESS_THREADS; tree $(git -C $FH rev-parse --short HEAD)$(git -C $FH diff --quiet HEAD -- ProjectFortress Library || echo ' with the next rung applied, not yet committed'); tests from $D"
clean () { for t in "$@"; do n=$(sed -n 's/^tests=//p' "$D/$t" | head -1); [ -n "$n" ] && find ../default_repository/caches -name "*$n*" -exec rm -rf {} + 2>/dev/null; done; }
clean "$@"
if [ -n "${ONE_JVM:-}" ]; then
  files=(); for t in "$@"; do files+=("$D/$t"); done
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit, one JVM: $*"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "${files[@]}" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
else
for t in "$@"; do
  echo "########## [$L] fortress junit $t"
  java $JAVA_FLAGS -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.Shell junit "$D/$t" 2>&1 | sed "s#$FH/##g" | grep -v '^\s*at ' | cut -c1-240
  echo "exit=${PIPESTATUS[0]}"
done
fi
clean "$@"

# Climb batch 15, rung C (rung-checker-bounds): the checker's normal form over a variable, and its local function groups

- problem: the distance stage's site `squaredNorm(me)`, 'Could not check call to function squaredNorm', and its crash row in `Array3` (`explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv:15`; `explorations/compile-ladder/climb-batch-14/gate/distance.txt:27`), with the four expected failures of rows 686, 687, 689 and 690 (`ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/XXX*TwoBoundsClosedTrait.test` at ee1aa1a95).
- spec: `Specification/basic/inference.tex:56-58` ("A declaration with static parameters is applicable to a call ... if some instance of it whose static arguments satisfy their bounds is applicable to the call"); for row 680, `Specification/basic/functions.tex:597-598` ("locally declared functions in a single scope are allowed to be overloaded and mutually recursive").
- precedent: the type-variable case of `pSubInner`, which reads a variable's bound through `pNorm` under a history entry (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala:200-236`), and its inference-variable case (`:189`); for row 680's held line, Thunker's priming of a trait's and an object's methods with a TryChecker over the checker that holds them (`ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/Thunker.scala:63-77`, `:103-116`).
- deviation: the team's expansion of a closed trait into its listed types is kept for a meet of ground types, which the type group's figures do not have: no rule of `Papers/Types/fig-subtype.tick:1-133` or `fig-meet.tick` reads a `comprises` clause (`TypeAnalyzer.scala:708-735`); no deviation from the probe's patches.
- historical: `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/types/TypeAnalyzer.scala` (`a874948ac`, `:632-641`); `ProjectFortress/src/com/sun/fortress/scala_src/typechecker/impls/Decls.scala` was edited and then put back to the base's text, so it is not edited on the branch.

## 1. What changed, and why

The base is ee1aa1a95. The branch holds one edit of the checker, in `TypeAnalyzer.scala`, from the checker probe's two patches (`explorations/perf-probes/checker-bound-defects/patches/rows-686-687-689-690-normal-form.patch` and `sibling-ground-bound.patch`), applied unchanged (`4356454a2`):

- **The normal form** (`normConjunct`, `TypeAnalyzer.scala:708-735`). A closed trait among the conjuncts of an intersection is replaced by the types its `comprises` clause lists that another conjunct excludes only where that conjunct names no type variable and no inference variable (`excludedListed`, `:713-714`). A bound such as `K ∩ R[\T\]` therefore stays the intersection as written, the redundancy branch drops `K` beside a `T` whose bound implies it, and no union the checker builds over such a bound holds a variable. This is the condition under which the POPL 2019 paper proves matching complete (`research/extracts/ParkPOPL2019-extract.md`, section 6), the type group's late word (P-26). Before the edit, `K ∩ R[\$T\]` became `OR(AND(A,R[$T]),AND(B,R[$T]))`, and the union rule split it before the variable's bound was read (the probe's section 2.2). One change clears rows 686, 687, 689 and 690.
- **The union cases** (`pSubInner`, `TypeAnalyzer.scala:165-180`, before the union rule at `:181-182`, both only where the check is not negated). An inference variable below a union takes the union as one upper bound (`:168`), so the inference-variable rule of `fig-subtype.tick` comes before its union rule. A type variable below a union is also tried through its bound, with the type-variable case's history entry (`:171-180`). This clears the ground sibling (NEW-C-1): `g[\T extends { K, Q }\](x: T): T = h(x)` with `trait Q excludes { C }`, where `K ∩ Q` is ground and still expanded to `OR(A,B)`. The solver then takes the intersection of the upper bounds, here the union, which is the bound: P-48.

Row 680's line (`row-680-local-function-group.patch`, `makeTryChecker(this)` to `makeTryChecker(newChecker)` in the `SLetFn` case, `impls/Decls.scala:414`) was applied, built and tested (`3216343f6`), and then held (`e75bb538b`). With it, and with `__bigOperator`'s `body(i)` typed for one run only, the count stage checked the library component whole and took 809 s, past the 690 s that the batch record sets for landing it (section 6). The line is valid and its tests passed on it (section 2). Its tests stay in the tree as expected failures keyed on today's crashes.

## 2. The tests: the failing run and the passing run

All are in `ProjectFortress/compiler_tests/`. They were written first (`d7bf79b07`) and run through the harness on the base's code before the edit was first built:
- a union or a generic `excludes`: `Exception`, `LabelTest`, `commonSuper`, `GenericFnWithExcludes`.

None is in the landed `ladder.tsv`, so each was compared with the baseline's. Ten are at the same phase with the same first error (`funny` and `simplify1` but for the tree's path). `commonSuper` and `GenericFnWithExcludes` are at the same phase, `typecheck`, with another first error that the old code gives too (section 5). No ladder file moved.

## 7. Sentences of the specification made false

None. The search: `grep -rn` over `Specification/` for rows 680 and 686 to 690, and for the messages 'Applied a substitution to an And and got an Or', 'TryChecker returned an untyped expr' and 'Result of typechecking still contains intermediate nodes'.

- The only hit is the rationale of `revival-paramtype` (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:3324-3329`). It gives the crash messages of rows 620 to 622 as history before that change, and it stays true. With row 680's line held, the crash it names still occurs at a sibling call.
- The Appendix I passages on row 518 (`changes.tex:1944-1946`: such an argument "was refused ... It now follows the chapter") and on row 695 (`:3570-3574`: the parameter "at an object type fails") stay true. `SelfTypeReturnSelfAtTraitRun` now guards the second from the other side.
- The entries on closed traits and covering (`changes.tex:2755-2770`, `:2858-2870`) speak of meets of ground traits, whose expansion the change keeps.
- `basic/inference.tex` and `advanced/overloading.tex` make no claim on the normal form.

## 8. Points to report

- **Count tables and row 680's line.** Run 1: 379 s, count 1. Run 3 (final): 378 s, count 1, the table equal to batch 14's. Run 2, the component's own errors: 43 in 809 s, past 690 s. **Row 680's line did not land** (`e75bb538b`). Evidence: section 6.
- **A patch changed from the probe's.** None. The normal-form and sibling patches are on the branch as the probe wrote them (`4356454a2`). Row 680's patch was applied unchanged and then held by the 690 s rule, not changed. `InferUnionInstanceArg` keeps its verdict, `PASS` (the passing run; `fast-compiler` 0 failures).
- **A site beyond `:2493` and the crash row.** None comes or goes. The crash row stays, its line held (section 6).
- **A compiled test whose verdict changes beyond the promotions and the new tests, or a ladder file that moves.** None (section 6).
- **A specification sentence made false.** None (section 7).
- **A checker file edited beyond the two, or a library or walk edit.** None on the branch. `impls/Decls.scala` was edited (`3216343f6`) and put back (`e75bb538b`). `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:1314` was changed for run 2 only, restored, and never committed.

## 9. Decisions

1. **Row 680's line held.** The count over the whole component took 809 s, past the record's 690 s (section 6, run 2).
   - Taken: the record's own rule, "If it prints no total or takes more than 690 s, do not land row 680's line: land the normal form and the sibling, and report" (`explorations/coordinator/CLIMB-BATCH-15.md:154`).
   - Not taken: landing it on the reading that the run's load (3 to 9 on 4 cores, beside other rungs' suites) explains the excess, since the 690 s margin was set for load.
   - Not taken: running the stage again on a quieter machine. The record makes run 2 "the batch's one measure of that stage", and a second try would choose among measures.
   - Not taken: the library's workaround `plane(k: ZZ32): () =`. The line is valid as written (the probe's section 4), and the library is not this rung's.
2. **Row 680's tests kept as expected failures**, keyed on today's crashes (home 2: the specification settles it, `basic/functions.tex:597-598`). Not taken: dropping them and handing them over, which leaves the row's reproducer `none`; plain tests, which would be red; expected failures with no key, which would stay green across the repair and so not show it.
3. **The recursive case keyed on its crash, not deleted.** When row 680's line lands it turns red, 'Did not satisfy compile_err_contains', and the repair re-keys it to `reference cycle`, the checker's rule for a cycle (`Thunker.scala:264`, `XXX5bn.test`). Not taken: deleting it until then; keying it on `reference cycle`, which is red today.
4. **The two code changes in two commits** (`4356454a2`, `3216343f6`), so that row 680's line could be held by one revert. Not taken: one commit, which a hold would have split.
5. **The promotions keep `compile`** beside `link` and `run`, as their neighbours `OverloadTwoBoundsClosedTrait` and `InferUnionInstanceArg` do. Not taken: `link` and `run` only, which the skill's run-time pair uses.
6. **Test names.** Each new name sits beside its family. Not taken: the probe's file names (`BoundsGround`, `LocalRecursiveUntyped`), which name no topic.
   - `CallerParamTwoGroundBoundsClosedTrait` for the sibling, beside `CallerParamTwoBoundsClosedTrait`, whose shape it shares with a ground second bound.
   - `XXXLocalFunctionRecursiveUntypedReturn`, beside the landed `XXXLocalFunctionUntypedParam*`.
   - `SelfTypeReturnSelfAtTraitRun`, beside `XXXSelfTypeReturnSelfRun`.
7. **The normal form keeps the team's expansion for ground meets** (the probe's decision, its section 10).
   - Not taken: removing the expansion. It also clears the sibling, but it was never run through the tracks and it changes every ground meet with a closed trait.
   - Not taken: a guard in `slv` (section 3).
   - No decision of the curator covers the analyzer's normal form. The reading acted on is P-26's POPL 2019 condition, which the change keeps.
8. **The ladder subset** is the 12 files of section 6. Not taken: an empty subset (no first error names the normal form); the whole ladder (the gate's).

## 10. Defects, each with its home

- **Rows 686, 687, 689, 690**: home 1, repaired (`4356454a2`). Tests: `InferCallerTwoBoundsClosedTrait`, `CoerceTwoBoundsClosedTrait`, `CallerParamTwoBoundsClosedTrait`, `ReturnRuleTwoBoundsClosedTrait`. The cause is the normal form over a variable (section 1). Row 686's claim also covers a ground second bound, whose face stays refused: it closes with its claim narrowed, and the ground face is NEW-C-2 (the skeptic's correction, `SKEPTIC.md`).
- **The ground sibling, NEW-C-1**: home 1, repaired (`4356454a2`). Test: `CallerParamTwoGroundBoundsClosedTrait`. A new row (record.md), to add and close at once.
- **Row 680**: home 2, deferred; its repair was measured and held. Tests: `XXXLocalFunctionSiblingInLoop` (its reproducer from now on) and `XXXLocalFunctionSiblingCall`. Its claim and its note "A compiler-world program of the same shape typechecks" are false. `plane`'s body is well typed; the group's thunks are primed without the group (`impls/Decls.scala:414`); and the two compiled tests crash the checker on the base. The corrected claim is in record.md.
- **The recursive local function with no return type**, 'Result of typechecking still contains intermediate nodes': row 680's mechanism, home 2 under row 680. Test: `XXXLocalFunctionRecursiveUntypedReturn`. With the line, it gets the cycle refusal.
- **Row 695's bound at a trait type**: no defect. `SelfTypeReturnSelfAtTraitRun` guards it.
- **What the normal form gives up** (the probe's section 2.4): the exclusion of a meet over a variable from a type that excludes each remaining listed type but neither conjunct. No test, track or site shows a case; the skeptic's program shows one, an overloading the base accepted and the head refuses, on a question that Appendix I lists as not settled: NEW-C-3, `XXXOverloadTwoBoundsClosedTraitExclusion` (`SKEPTIC.md`).
- **A self-bounded type parameter that no argument fixes** (the skeptic's measure, `SKEPTIC.md`): `mk(A)` for `mk[\T extends R[\T\]\](x: K)` is refused as not applicable on the base and the head; with `{ K, R[\T\] }` as the bound the base crashed and the head refuses. Home 2: NEW-C-4, `XXXInferUnfixedSelfBoundedParam`.

## 11. For FACTS

record.md holds the new fact on the normal form and the union cases, and the corrections of F-94, F-53 and F-54.

## 12. Commands worked out

- The count stage's time, which its table does not print: the brief's nohup line with `s=$(date +%s)` before `run.sh` and `echo "# seconds $(( $(date +%s) - s ))"` after it, and a machine line first.
- The per-site comparison: `diff <(grep -v '^#' explorations/compile-ladder/gate/distance-sites.tsv | cut -f1,4,6,7 | sort) <(grep -v '^#' tmp/rung-checker-bounds/dist-post/errors.tsv | cut -f1,4,6,7 | sort)`.
- The ladder subset's comparison with the baseline, file by file: `awk -F'\t'` over the baseline's and the run's `ladder.tsv`, columns 4 (phase) and 11 (first error).

content.content:
#!/bin/bash
# harness-one.sh <scratch-dir> <file.fss>... : rung C's harness-one.sh (explorations/compile-ladder/
# rung-interp-coercion/, itself rung I's shape): the testSystem harness (SystemJUTest, the class build.xml's
# testSystem shards run) over a directory holding only the named test files, with the JVM settings of
# build.xml's systemShard macro and a private cache. Run from FORTRESS_HOME with explorations/experiment/env.sh.
#
# The scratch directory is deleted when the call starts and when it ends. The private cache is the folder
# <scratch-dir>.cache beside it, kept between calls. A call starts from what that folder holds when it was
# filled under the implementation now built (ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp, which ant compileAll
# writes) and from the Fortress sources now on the source path outside the scratch directory (the .fss and
# .fsi files of Library, ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin, ProjectFortress/test_library and ProjectFortress);
# otherwise it empties the folder first. COLD_CACHE=1 empties it in any case. The folder is stamped only when
# the JVM ends normally, so a call that is killed leaves it to be emptied by the next one.
set -u
S=$(realpath -m -- "${1:?scratch dir}") ; shift
FH=${FORTRESS_HOME:?}
C=$S.cache
BUILT=$FH/ProjectFortress/build/implementation.stamp
sources_key () {
    ( cd "$FH" && { find Library ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin ProjectFortress/test_library -type f -name '*.fs[si]' -print0
                    find ProjectFortress -maxdepth 1 -type f -name '*.fs[si]' -print0 ; } \
        | sort -z | xargs -0 -r sha1sum | sha1sum | cut -c1-40 )
}
key () { [ -f "$BUILT" ] && echo "$(head -1 "$BUILT") sources $(sources_key)" ; }
rm -rf "$S" ; mkdir -p "$S/tests" "$S/tmp"
KEY=$(key)
if [ -z "${COLD_CACHE:-}" ] && [ -n "$KEY" ] && [ "$(cat "$C/harness.stamp" 2>/dev/null)" = "$KEY" ]; then
    CACHE=filled
else
    rm -rf "$C" ; mkdir -p "$C" ; printf '\0\0\0\0' > "$C/global.map" ; CACHE=empty

fi
rm -f "$C/harness.stamp"
for f in "$@" ; do cp "$f" "$S/tests/" ; done
CP=$("$FH/bin/fortress_classpath" 2>/dev/null | tail -1)
echo "# harness-one $(date -u +%FT%TZ); tree $(git -C "$FH" rev-parse --short HEAD); nproc=$(nproc); load $(cut -d' ' -f1-3 /proc/loadavg); $(java -version 2>&1 | head -1); FORTRESS_THREADS=4; cache $CACHE"
cd "$FH/ProjectFortress" && FORTRESS_THREADS=4 FORTRESS_JUNIT_VERBOSE=1 FORTRESS_CACHES="$C" \
  java -Xmx768m -Xss32m -Djava.io.tmpdir="$S/tmp" -Dfortress.caches="$C" -Dtests="$S/tests" \
       -Dfile.encoding=UTF-8 -cp "$CP" com.sun.fortress.tests.unit_tests.SystemJUTest 2>&1 | grep -v '^\s*at ' | sed "s#$FH/##g"
RC=${PIPESTATUS[0]}
echo "exit=$RC"
# The cache is stamped only if the run ended normally and nothing it is keyed on changed meanwhile.
[ "$RC" = 0 ] && [ -n "$KEY" ] && [ "$(key)" = "$KEY" ] && echo "$KEY" > "$C/harness.stamp"
rm -rf "$S"

## 7. The specification's text, and the sentences made false

Changed in the S1 form (P-96), in place:

- The revival box `revival-overloading` on Jan's pair in the internal document (`Specification/appendices/future.tex:257-268`): the factory chooses "a \TYP{Vector} where the argument is one of the eight number types \TYP{ZZ32}, ..., and a plain array where it is any other type, \TYP{Number} among them, since a \TYP{Vector} of \TYP{Number} is not well-formed under the bound that \library\ give the element type of a \TYP{Vector} (\secref{type-param})". It said "a \TYP{Vector} where the argument is a \TYP{Number}".
- Appendix I, "Overloading with static parameters": its Change records the revision with its reason (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2402-2409`), and its Original text keeps the box's former last clause (`:2567-2571`). Its sentence that Jan's example is answered by the library's factory (`:2414-2417`) stays true. Its Effect is rung O's.

Made false and not edited here:

- `Specification/basic/expressions/aggregate.tex:165-166`, "A one-dimensional array whose elements are a subtype of \TYP{Number} is a vector.", and `:152-155`, "An array of two dimensions whose elements are a subtype of \TYP{Number} is a matrix.": false now for `array1` and `array2` at `Number`, `AnyIntegral` or any element type other than the eight, and at walk's `Int`. They were already false for the library's other arrays, `primitiveArray`, the immutable arrays and every view (row 54), and they cannot hold for `Number` itself under the library's bound on `Vector` (F-151). They are normative text, not a box or an Effect, and no decision says which side gives way (section 11).
- FACTS F-151, "The checker still refuses the first factories' results (row 685) and the norm's call (row 686).": its row 685 half is false with this rung.
- None in an Appendix I Effect or a `\note`: `grep -n 'Vector\|vector' Specification/appendices/changes.tex` names only this entry's lines; `grep -rn 'IntMap\|UPLUS' Specification --include=*.tex` names the operator tables only (`Specification/appendices/operators.tex:328`, `:1355`; `Specification/basic/operators/opr-overview.tex:226`).
- In the skill, none: `references/revival-changes.md` speaks of `IntMap`'s `SYMDIFF` only, and `references/library.md:26` of `fill` and `tabulate`.

The front matter's paragraph on the revision (`Specification/fortress/preamble.tex:54-64`) stays true. The section asked for no decision record; the reasoning is here.

## 8. Points to report

- **A walk value that changes, `array1` and `array2` at an abstract number type:** `array1[\Number,2\]()`, `array1[\AnyIntegral,2\]()`, `array2[\Number,2,2\]()` and `array[\Number\](3)` give plain arrays where they gave a `Vector` or a `Matrix` (`ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayFactoryAbstractNumber.fss:6-9`).
- **A walk value that changes, at walk's run-time class:** an array that `array`, `array1` or `array2` builds at a `T` that walk instantiates at `Int` from a `ZZ32` value is plain where it was a `Vector[\Int,n\]`; its `+` and unary `-`, which the base ran, now find no overload (section 6; `ProjectFortress/tests/XXXArrayInferredElementVectorWalk.fss:10`). The probe's patch threw `CastError` there instead.
- **Each `IntMap` test whose value or throw changes:** `IntMapUplusSingleton.fss:24-25` (the pins, below); the new `IntMapUplusManyEntry.fss:23-24` and `IntMapComprehensionRepeatedKey.fss:17-28`, each red on the base. A comprehension or map expression with a repeated key throws `KeyOverlap` in every order (`IntMapComprehensionRepeatedKey.fss:17-26`); one whose key repeats with the same value throws too (section 6). The team's `IntMapTest` and `IntMapCombine` hold no repeated key and keep their values.
- **Each repair's precedent line:** `additiveIdentity` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fss:3229-3244` at ee1aa1a95, `:3245-3260` now), with the witness taken of the result type (the deviation above); `NodeIM`'s `addNew` (`Library/IntMap.fss:488-490`) and `SingletonIM`'s `UPLUS` by `addNew` (`:339-340`).
- **Each team line changed:** `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2451-2456` at ee1aa1a95 (the team's comment "TODO: fix when Number is covariant", the `typecase __thrower[\T\]` and its arm `() -> Number => vector[\T,s0\]()`), now `:2451-2465`; `:2823-2828` at ee1aa1a95 (the same comment and `()->Number => matrix[\T,s0,s1\]()`), now `:2832-2844`; `Library/IntMap.fss:520`, `self.add(other)`, now `self.addNew(other)`. The team's `else` arms and its comment "array2 is a factory for 0-based 2-D arrays." are kept.
- **The pins changed in `IntMapUplusSingleton.fss`:**
  - `:24` before: `assert(overlap(fn () => three UPLUS one), "no exception", "today's value: a many-entry map UPLUS a one-entry map holding its key throws nothing")`; after: `assert(overlap(fn () => three UPLUS one), "IntMap.KeyOverlap: 1 |-> 1 and |-> 9", "a many-entry map UPLUS a one-entry map holding its key throws KeyOverlap")`.
  - `:25` before: `assert(three UPLUS one, three, "today's value: a many-entry map UPLUS a one-entry map holding its key keeps the many-entry map's entries")`; after: `assert(overlap(fn () => three UPLUS one), overlap(fn () => one UPLUS three), "a many-entry map UPLUS a one-entry map holding its key throws as the reverse order does")`.
  - `:1`, the header comment, before: "IntMap's UPLUS of a many-entry map and a one-entry map on a shared key, whose value under walk throws KeyOverlap only with the one-entry map on the left."; after: "IntMap's UPLUS of a many-entry map and a one-entry map throws KeyOverlap on a shared key in either order, and holds every entry otherwise."
- **A site that comes or goes beyond row 685's four:** none; 54 to 50, the four gone and no site new (section 3).
- **Normative text changed:** the revival box in the internal document (`Specification/appendices/future.tex:264-268`) and its Appendix I entry's Change and Original text (`Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2402-2409`, `:2569-2571`); the sentences made false are in section 7.
- **A checker or walk edit:** none.
- **Of the same kind, a repair that departs from the patch the section names:** the witness of the result type in place of the probe's witness of `T` (section 4; `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:2455`, `:2834`).
- **Of the same kind, a defect outside the rung's files given a test:** `openRange`'s `CastError` at walk's `Int` (`ProjectFortress/tests/XXXOpenRangeInferredIndexWalk.fss:10`; `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:4076-4079`).

## 9. Decisions

1. **The witness of the result type (way 3), not the probe's patch as written (way 1).** Ways not taken: way 1, which throws `CastError` for a statically well-formed call at a type below a number type, `Int` among them, and so in walk's generic code at an inferred `T` (section 4, measured); way 2, which throws the same and adds two declarations (measured in a shadow copy); way 4, a language change. Evidence: the `CastError` runs of section 4; the base runs `filled(z)`; the compiled checker accepts way 3's shape (section 4), and the stages confirm it (section 3). The section says to apply the probe's patch and own it; this keeps its arms, its eight types, its `cast` and its `else` arms, and changes only what the `typecase` tests. No decision of the curator covers the choice of witness.
2. **The team's TODO comment is replaced, not kept.** Kept, it would say the factory waits on `Number` becoming covariant, which no longer describes the code. Way not taken: keeping it beside the new comment.
3. **`IntMapUplusSingleton.fss:25` asserts that both orders throw alike**, where the pinned value no longer exists. Ways not taken: deleting the line (the skill keeps every assertion), or asserting the message a second time.
4. **The `KeyOverlap` messages of many-entry maps and comprehensions are asserted as one of their possible forms**, the repeated key with its two values in either order, since which repeated key `nodeNode`'s recursion meets first, and in which role, is not something the library promises. Way not taken: pinning the message one run printed (the same at 1 and 4 threads).
5. **The array tests use `instanceOf[\AnyVector\]` and `instanceOf[\AnyMatrix\]` for "plain"**, so no test names an ill-formed `Vector[\Number,2\]`. Way not taken: the probe's `typecase` against `Vector[\RR64,2\]`, which a `String` array never meets anyway.
6. **The run-time-class consequence is recorded as an expected failure** (home 2), since the specification instantiates `ZZ32` there. Way not taken: a test pinning walk's plain array with a new row (home 3); the departure is row 364's, so its note names the test.
7. **`openRange`'s `CastError` gets an expected failure and a note, not a repair**, since `openRange` is not in this rung's files. Way not taken: repairing it here by the result type's witness.
8. **The same-value repeated key is not asserted** in any test, since the text names only a different value (section 5). Way not taken: pinning the throw, which `Map` also gives.
9. **The ladder subset is the seven files whose recorded first error names a factory this change touched in the other library**, since none of the baseline's `raw/` names one; run to show they do not move.
10. **The probe programs ran against a shadow copy of the library before the edit**, not against an edit of the tracked file, so the tests' failing runs came first (the skill's "The order", step 2). Way not taken: editing the library and reverting it.

## 10. Defects, each with its home

- **Row 685** (the factories at an unbounded `T`): home 1, repaired; `ArrayFactoryAbstractNumber` and the two stages. Closed with its claim and class corrected to the library line (`record.md`).
- **Row 704** (`UPLUS` keeps a value on a shared key in one order): home 1, repaired; `IntMapUplusSingleton`, `IntMapUplusManyEntry`, `IntMapComprehensionRepeatedKey`. Closed.
- **720** (the checker reports a call's static argument that fails the callee's bound at the callee's declared type): home 3, a row only, as the section asks. Its reproducer, `explorations/perf-probes/checker-bound-defects/repro/FactoryUnboundedCaller.fss`, gives on this tree, under `bin/fortress typecheck`, "FactoryUnboundedCaller.fss:11:42-48: Ill-formed type: V[\T,s0\]" twice (against `K` and `R[\T\]`): line 11 is `vec`'s declared result, and the call is on line 16.
- **The factories' array at walk's inferred `Int`** (plain, where the specification gives a vector): home 2, `XXXArrayInferredElementVectorWalk`; row 364's departure, so a note on row 364.
- **`openRange` at walk's inferred `Int`** (`CastError`): home 2, `XXXOpenRangeInferredIndexWalk`; a note on row 364. It was there on the base.
- **The probe patch's `CastError`** at a type below a number type: not landed, so not a defect of the tree; section 4 keeps it.

## 11. For the curator

- **The vector and matrix sentences of "Array Expressions".** "A one-dimensional array whose elements are a subtype of \TYP{Number} is a vector." (`Specification/basic/expressions/aggregate.tex:165-166`) and the matrix sentence (`:152-155`) cannot hold at `Number` under the library's bound on `Vector` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1613`; F-151), and walk now gives a plain array there (`ProjectFortress/tests/ArrayFactoryAbstractNumber.fss:6`). Should the text say "whose element type is one of the number types" (with a box and an Appendix I entry), or does the library's bound give way? Default: the text as it stands, the departure listed here, for the gather or a later text rung.
- **A key repeated with the same value in a map comprehension.** The text throws `KeyOverlap` where a key repeats with a different value (`Specification/basic/expressions/comprehensions.tex:78-80`) and says nothing of the same value; `Map`'s comprehension (`Library/Map.fss:161-168`) and now every `IntMap` comprehension throw on any repeated key ("IntMap.KeyOverlap: 0 |-> 7 and |-> 7" for `{k MOD 3 |-> 7 | k <- 0#4}`, section 6). Default: the libraries' throw, untested.

6:- The reason: the library bounds a vector's element type by `{ Number, MultiplicativeRing[\T\] }` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:1613`), which `Number`, `AnyIntegral` and `Int` do not meet, so `Vector[\Number,n\]` is not a well-formed type (`Specification/basic/inference.tex:56-58`), and the compiled checker, run over the interpreter's library, refused the team's call four times: "Ill-formed type: Vector[\T,s0\] The static argument T does not satisfy the corresponding bound Number.", the same against `MultiplicativeRing[\T\]`, and both again for `Matrix[\T,s0,s1\]`. A witness of the element type would match a type below a number type and throw `CastError` at the `cast` (measured at `Int`: "CastError" at `Library/FortressLibrary.fss:36:13-27`); the witness of the result type matches exactly.
11:- The reason: the library's own comment, "%UPLUS% (disjoint union) throws the %KeyOverlap% exception when a key occurs in both maps." (`Library/IntMap.fss:517-518`), and the one-entry map's `UPLUS`, which already threw (`:339-340`). The specification throws `KeyOverlap` for a map comprehension whose key repeats with a different value (`Specification/basic/expressions/comprehensions.tex:78-80`), and `Map`'s comprehension throws on any repeated key (`Library/Map.fss:161-168`).

## 7. Sentences made false

Corrected by the rung:
- `Specification/appendices/changes.tex:2500-2502` (before): "except two functional methods whose \KWD{self} parameters stand at different positions, which only its code generator refuses, as a malformed overload set (row~707 ...)".
- `changes.tex:2876-2880` (before): "and it does not refuse an object where its search through the \KWD{comprises} clauses does not settle ... (row~708 ...)".
- `changes.tex:2881-2885` (before): "The compiled type checker does not split a tuple of parameter types through \KWD{comprises} clauses ... (row~709 ...)".

Now false, for the gather; record.md gives the new text for the FACTS entries:
- FACTS F-145: "A search for a cover that does not settle does not refuse (row 708) ... The compiled checker misses a cover through the listed types of two parameters (row 709)."
- FACTS F-223: its title's "except between functional methods whose `self` parameters stand at different positions", and "A pair at different positions passes it, and the code generator then stops the compile (row 707)."
- The skill, `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/interpreter.md:42`: "If walk's search for a cover does not settle, it does not refuse."
- The skill, `.claude/skills/fortress-repo/references/revival-changes.md:66`: "If walk's search for a cover does not settle, walk does not refuse the object (ledger row 708). The compiled checker misses a cover that needs the listed types of two parameters together (ledger row 709)."

Not affected:
- No note in the chapters names these departures: `grep -rn "malformed\|self parameters stand\|settle" Specification/basic Specification/advanced` finds none on them.
- The Effect of "Overloading with static parameters" does not say that the checker checks no symbolic operator (row 584). It did not say so before the rung either; the rung's sentence makes that no truer and no falser.

## 8. Points to report

- **The message row 707's refusal prints** (`OverloadingChecker.scala:444-451`):
  - Both declarations' spans, then "There are multiple declarations of f with the same parameter type: ", then the domain of the declaration written first: without its self parameter in a trait's or object's check, whole in the top-level set.
  - The generic pair prints `(S, T)` (top level) and `(T)` (trait `S`, and object `O`, which provides both; one message); two errors.
  - The plain pair prints `(S, S)` and `(S)`.
  - Before the message edit the domain was that of the declaration the check met second in a set's order. It varied between runs: the harness run of `317fc0ef5` printed `(S, T)`, `(T)`, `(U)`; a direct compile printed `(U, S)` and `(U)`. Now three runs, two direct and one in the harness, print `(S, T)` and `(T)`.
  - `XXXNoDuplicatesRule` now prints `Box[\T\]` where it printed `Box[\U\]`. Its key is unchanged, and so is its verdict.
- **The bound row 709's split takes** (`AbstractMethodChecker.scala:125-126`): 10,000 steps and 4,096 combinations of parts, walk's `OVERLAP_STEPS` and `OVERLAP_PARTS` (`OverloadedFunction.java:865`, `:868`). Past them the object is refused. Row 708's shape, 6^5 = 7,776 combinations, is refused by both paths.
- **A library, team or test declaration newly refused:** none. `ant testQuick` and `ant testSystem` are green, and the count's table did not move.
  - The library's pairs at two self positions, found with `grep -nE "\(\s*[^)]*[a-zA-Z_0-9']+\s*:[^)]*,\s*self\s*[,)]" Library/*.fs? ProjectFortress/LibraryBuiltin/*.fs?`:
    - `FlatString`'s `opr ||(self, b:FlatString)` and `opr ||(a:FlatString, self)` (`Library/FlatString.fsi:17`, `:20`), which are equivalent;
    - `String`'s `||`, `|||`, `//`, `///` at `(self, b:Any)` and `(a:Any, self)` (`Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:2494-2495`, `:2501-2502`, `:2507-2508`, `:2513-2514`), which are not equivalent.
  - The check reaches none of these, since it checks no symbolic operator (`isDeclaredName`, row 584).
  - The word-named functional methods with self not first are `IN`, `NOTIN` and `MATCH`, for example `Library/FortressLibrary.fsi:691`, `:695` and `Library/GeneratorLibrary.fsi:16-17`. None has a same-named sibling with self first: `grep -nE "opr\s+(IN|NOTIN|MATCH)\s*\(\s*self"` prints nothing.
- **A test whose verdict changes other than the three tests of the rows:** none. No ladder file moved.
- **A count or distance site that moves:** none (section 6).
- **Text beyond the three Appendix I sentences:** one Effect sentence added in the same entry, on 725 (`changes.tex:2885-2888`); it is not normative. The sentences made false are in section 7, the skill's two among them.
